deltas.description: h>=0 is an exposed necessary restriction for the descent route and arbitrary-comparator energy claim.
deltas.evidence: Take f(t)=t^2/2 on R, beta=1,h=-1,x=1. The printed h<=1/beta holds; T(1)=2 and f(2)-f(1)=3/2 exceeds -(h/2)|grad f(1)|^2=1/2. Take f(t)=t^2/2, alpha=1/2,beta=1,h=-1,x=0,z=1. This f is alpha-strongly convex and beta-smooth. T(0)=0; ||T(0)-1||^2+2h(f(T(0))-f(1))=2 while (1-alpha h)||0-1||^2=3/2. Thus the printed arbitrary-comparator claim fails.

deltas.description: Whole production module, including private step_descent, was reviewed and source coverage is explicit.
deltas.evidence: Reviewed the entire private theorem statement and every proof line, not merely the exported conclusions. It assumes h>=0, beta h<=1 and the global quadratic upper model at the gradient symbol. Evaluating that model at s=x-h grad f(x) gives f(s)-f(x)<=-h||g||^2+(beta/2)h^2||g||^2. Multiplying beta h<=1 by h||g||^2>=0 proves descent. No beta>=0 or C1 premise is required for this purely algebraic implication from the already supplied upper model. In both public consumers C1 guarantees the gradient is the genuine derivative, recovering the intended source calculus setting. The helper is explained explicitly in both lesson proof chains, as an implementation of Lemma3.1 rather than an independently registered theorem.

deltas.description: q>=0 is explicit; q=0 extends source positive-coefficient recurrence through division-free products.
deltas.evidence: For k<N, g_N<=g_(k+1); multiplication by -2h<=0 reverses this inequality. Multiplication by q^(N-(k+1))>=0 then preserves it. Summing, reversing k and discarding u_N>=0 gives precisely 2h S_N g_N<=q^N u0. No bound q<=1 is needed. N=0 has S0=0, q^0=1 and yields 0<=||x0-z||^2. h=0 gives T=id, q=1 and a zero left coefficient. q=0 gives S_N=1 and q^N=0 for N>=1 without reciprocal evaluation. q=1 gives S_N=N. q>1, possible with negative alpha, is valid though not a decaying optimization rate.
